name: mask-gated marker scan
summary: Selector 0 inspects the actor lane bitmask against the configured lane count and scans for the next 0x01 marker. Selectors 1 and 2 are marker-aware continuation forms.
operands: payload selector; selector 0 has no scalar operand
control_flow: returns a cursor; selector 0 can skip nested instructions and consume an extra 0x01 marker

name: tracked-player check
summary: Selector 0 executes the body when actor+2687 is nonzero; otherwise it clears the current target index and scans to else/end.
operands: payload selector; selector 0 has no scalar operand
control_flow: conditional nested-body skip with target-clear side effect on false
writes: actor+2612 = 0xFF only when selector is 0 and actor+2687 is zero

variants.summary: check tracked players; clear current target on false

name: check_pending_area
summary: Selector 0 enters the body only when pending area actor+2046 differs from current area actor+2040, is not 0xFFFF and passes the native species/map allowed-area table. Every false path clears the current and saved target-command tuples, then scans to else/end. Only rejection by the allowed-area table also restores actor+2046 to the current area; equal-area and 0xFFFF paths do not write it. DSL: if self.check_pending_area() { ... }, with optional else and nesting.
control_flow: selector 0 evaluates the condition and preserves native false-path cleanup; selector 1 skips else to the matching end; selector 2 continues after the condition
writes: actor+2581/actor+2582/actor+2584 cleared on every false path
actor+3231/actor+3232/actor+3234 cleared on every false path
actor+2046=current area only when a different non-0xFFFF pending area is rejected by the allowed-area table

variants.summary: begin: validate pending area and clear target-command tuples on false
else: skip to the matching end, not a frame wait

domain_notes: The candidate area is actor+2046, not the selected next-area cache at actor+3208. The handler does not clear actor+2612 or actor+3208.

The allowed-area list is selected by actor species and mapped global map index, not by interpreter stage or player slot. Entries at least 10000 compare directly after subtracting 10000; other entries use the native area-adaptation helpers.
DSL requires empty parentheses and only permits this method as an if condition. Empty bodies and omitted else clauses still evaluate the condition; no implicit 0x17, 0x18 or extra clear is generated.
Complete losslessly expressible blocks decompile to the method; other valid native layouts remain native(...). This ordinary opcode is distinct from the FF 03 table-9 subscript return.

name: reset-main-cursor
summary: Clears actor+2576 (main-table index) to 0 and loads main[0][0] through 0x10860340; the lane mask, delay and trigger latch are not touched.
control_flow: returns the selected main script cursor

name: dispatch-action
summary: Reads a three-byte action tuple (group, id, parameter), optionally invokes the action dispatcher, and stores the continuation cursor according to the active continuation flags.
operands: u8 group, u8 action_id, u8 parameter
control_flow: does not return a handler cursor; exits the current dispatch pass after saving continuation

variants.summary: opcode plus group, action id, parameter

name: select-script-target
summary: Configures the current target kind and its two arguments. Mode 3 adapts a u16 area, stores the pending area and invalidates the next-area cache; mode 10 derives an area from the selected player (or self); mode 13 scans eligible monster records. Other modes store their arguments for the target resolver. This does not execute a movement action. DSL exposes canonical player/point/area/direction/monster forms, including mode 2/group 3 as self.select_target_point(PointTarget::Landing, index) and group 4 as self.select_target_point(PointTarget::Departure, index). These select preparation points without performing landing, departure or takeoff.
operands: mode selector followed by mode-specific bytes; mode 3 carries a big-endian u16 id
control_flow: returns a cursor after the mode payload; mode 13 searches up to 40 actor records

variants.summary: mode 10 uses current lane to derive target id

domain_notes: 0x108538B0 resolves the stored target kind: 2 selects current-area point tables, 5 indexes the species fixed-point table, 7 looks up an explicit object, 8 uses the cached object point, 9 uses area-path act/step data, and 11 uses player-ground-point offsets. The setter alone does not resolve those positions.

Current DSL covers mode 1/group 0 player slots; mode 2/group 0 default, group 1 indexed route points, group 3 indexed Landing points and group 4 indexed Departure points; mode 3 canonical area form; eight mode-6 directions; mode 10 canonical player-area form; mode 13 subtypes 0..3 with zero trailing byte. Other byte layouts remain native.

Mode 2/groups 3 and 4 later resolve through point tables at actor+2900 -> +12 and +16 respectively. 0x108577B0 includes global fallback-point lookup; the resolver then tries the generic 0x118C0898 table and finally group 0 default if no point remains. Group 4 changes the group at 0x10853CB5..0x10853CC6. The DSL preserves these fallbacks without validating table length.

PointTarget::Landing and PointTarget::Departure each require an explicit index in the complete u8 range 0..255, emitting 06 02 03 index and 06 02 04 index respectively. Missing, empty or extra arguments are rejected. Every such layout decompiles to the corresponding method with the index preserved. They only write the current target kind/arguments, without an implicit resolve, movement, takeoff, landing or area transfer. Default, numeric route-point and Direction forms keep their existing encodings and argument counts.

The landing-preparation role is supported by Rathian aerial action flow 2:7 to 2:1 and by native area-transfer actions 2:9/2:11 constructing the tuple (2, 3, 0). The point selector itself does not perform these actions.

The Departure role is supported by Rathian map-31 sub_22_3 selecting group 4 before turn 1:3, movement 1:0, destination 300 and actions 2:0/2:8. Chameleos 59 at 0x1174B1FF and Kushala Daora 54/Tigrex 76 at 0x11754906/0x11729728 also use it before destination selection and departure; the latter scripts can skip approach when already near. This supports departure preparation without asserting one universal takeoff animation.

The numeric select_target_area form emits canonical 06 mode 3 and invalidates actor+3208. It is not folded into bind_target_area (1A), which immediately fills that cache; later native kind-3 resolution may converge and still select intermediate connected areas.

name: main-index-jump

name: in_area
summary: Selector 0 compares current area actor+2040 with the big-endian payload area ID normalized through 0x10B4C5E0; equality enters the body, otherwise skips to else/end. DSL: self.in_area(id).
operands: selector; selector 0 carries big-endian u16 area ID
control_flow: conditional body/else/end: selector 1 skips to matching end; selector 2 ends the condition

name: start-route-context
summary: Stores route-selection mode and script indices, saves the continuation for the active lane, enables the base route lane and resets route progress. For modes 0..2, resolves the current-area point table, records the requested count and available range, and transfers to root[2][payload[3]]. This changes script control flow rather than merely selecting a target. DSL keeps native(...).
operands: u8 mode, u8 requested count, u8 selection-source index, u8 entry-script index, u8 route-action script index
control_flow: saves cursor after all five payload bytes; enables lane bit 0x01; returns root[2][entry-script] for modes 0..2, original continuation when no point-table entry exists, or null when root[2] is absent; other modes return the existing base-lane cursor
domain_notes: For modes other than 1, a requested count greater than the table count is clamped to that count.
The saved continuation is written to +2604 for lane 0x20, +2596 for lane 0x10, +2588 for lane 0x01, otherwise +2548; the route-entry cursor then occupies +2588.
actor+2595 is em->cmd_route_act, the root[2] route-action script index consumed by route_ptr_set and FF FD/FE; all five payload bytes precede the continuation.

name: bind-route-waypoint
summary: For route modes 0/1/2, increments actor+3250 and reselects actor+2840 only when it is 0xFF or outside the signed available range. Mode 0 uses actor+1096 modulo the point count; mode 1 reads the first byte at root[2][actor+2593]; mode 2 selects zero. Finally binds target kind 2, group 1 and the selected waypoint. It does not advance the waypoint on every execution. DSL keeps native(...).
control_flow: normally updates target context and returns the supplied continuation; an empty mode-0 range can request and run native restart cleanup
writes: actor+2659=2 on empty mode-0 range when both gate bytes are zero
domain_notes: The selection counter is actor+1096, not actor+68; actor+3250 counts selection attempts and does not itself become the waypoint index.
Mode 1 requires a valid root[2] selection source; the native null-table path dereferences address zero.
Mode 0 builds a fixed-size native candidate buffer, so this operation should be modeled together with validated route-table metadata.

name: pick-highest-mask-lane
summary: Scans actor+2821 for set bits, stores the highest matching lane index, and sets the current action mode to 1/group 0.
writes: actor+2673 when not in gated state

name: pick-mask-lane-and-bind
summary: Scans the tracked-player mask actor+2687 and binds the highest set player-slot index to the action target and actor+2612, clearing two continuation/event flags. It is a tracked-slot selection, not a highest-hate-score comparison. DSL: self.select_target_entity(EntityTarget::TrackedPlayer).

name: bind-current-lane
summary: Sets action mode 1/group 0 and uses actor+2612 (cmd_pl_target) as the current index, masking it to four bits unless it is -1.

name: angle-threshold gate
summary: Selector 0 requires current target kind +2581 to be 1 or 13, arg1 +2582 to be zero and index +2584 to differ from 0xffff. It computes the shortest absolute XZ angle to the target relative to heading +164 and enters the body when that angle is greater than or equal to the payload threshold in integer degrees; otherwise skips to else/end. DSL: self.target_angle_at_least(degrees), with the complete u8 range 0..255.
operands: selector; selector 0 carries u8 integer degrees (0..255), converted to native angle units as floor(degrees * 65536 / 360 + 0.5)
control_flow: selector 0 begins the condition; selector 1 is else and skips to the matching end; selector 2 ends the condition
reads: actor+3231 saved kind used by 0x10855B30 to select the target array
selected target position and area coordinate adjustment

variants.summary: begin: valid target context and absolute horizontal angle >= integer-degree threshold

domain_notes: The absolute angle is folded into 0..32768 native units (0..180 degrees), so 180 includes directly behind and 181..255 are false. Threshold zero still requires valid target context. The compiler retains these byte values without clamping or constant folding.

Pure condition: no state writes, target binding or target resolution. The current-kind guard and saved-kind target lookup are preserved separately; there is no added same-area, alive or visible check.

Complete representable blocks decompile to the DSL with optional else and nesting, preserving every threshold byte. Legal layouts that cannot be represented losslessly remain native. Unlike 0x78, the payload is integer degrees and the angle is unsigned with respect to left versus right.

name: area_match
summary: Matches actor+2040 against big-endian u16 area cases in source order, applying native map adaptation to both sides. First match wins; else is optional. DSL: match self.area.
operands: selector; selector 0 carries count and big-endian u16 ids
control_flow: selector 0 conditionally skips nested body; selector 1 repeatedly advances to 0x15 subtype 3

variants.summary: logical count header; followed by a separate selector-1 branch marker and its big-endian u16 operand

domain_notes: variants.length records the logical linear instruction width; native_skip_length records the distinct 0x10860730 cursor increment, which includes the first branch marker for selector 0.

name: call_table9_subscript
summary: Calls root[9][index], storing the continuation in actor+2608 and the index in actor+2613. FF 03 restores that single cursor; neither instruction changes stage. Another 0x16 overwrites the saved continuation. DSL calls a function assigned to table 9.
control_flow: direct cursor replacement when the table exists; one saved return cursor, not a stack

name: init_area_change
summary: Only when actor+2844 is 0xFF, stores the root[5] area-list index, list count, root[6] area-handler index and end policy, then resets the selected-list index to 0xFF. The count is compared as i8: only raw values 2..127 remain; 0, 1 and 128..255 restore the uninitialized 0xFF sentinel while the other configuration bytes are still stored. Does not start an area change; opcode 0x18 uses this configuration. DSL: self.init_area_change(list, count, handler, end_policy), with all four u8 operands preserved exactly.
operands: u8 root[5] area-list index, u8 list count, u8 root[6] handler index, u8 end policy
control_flow: linear initialization; consumes all four payload bytes without writes when actor+2844 != 0xFF
domain_notes: actor+2614 indexes root[5] area lists; actor+2615 indexes root[6] scripts entered by opcode 0x18. DSL references existing native table indices without defining either table.

The fourth payload byte at actor+2620 is the end policy used by FF FB only when i8(actor+2844) <= i8(actor+2845): zero sets both fields to 0xFF; nonzero keeps the count and sets the selected index to zero. This does not establish a complete patrol-loop contract.
The count is compared as a signed byte both during initialization and by area-selection helpers; initialization is not an unconditional overwrite.
DSL accepts full 0..255 values for each operand, does not normalize the policy to a boolean and does not add an implicit area-change attempt, target bind or movement.

name: try_change_area
summary: When the area-route entry count is greater than one and the global gate allows it, selects a destination area, saves the continuation, and enters the configured root[6] script. DSL: self.try_change_area(); no result or immediate area-change guarantee.
control_flow: may replace the current cursor with the selected target script

name: bind-next-area
summary: Copies the already selected next area actor+3208 (maji_next_stage_no) to target kind 3/group/index, then calls the native no-op hook. It neither chooses a new area nor moves the actor or writes the current area. DSL keeps native(...).
domain_notes: Unlike 0x1A, has no explicit area operand, performs no area-ID normalization and does not write actor+2046 or actor+3208.
Target resolution/action execution remains separate from this binding.

name: bind-target-area
summary: Reads a big-endian u16 area ID, adapts it through 0x10B4C5E0, and writes the result to pending area actor+2046, next-area cache actor+3208 and current target arguments actor+2582/+2584 with kind actor+2581=3. DSL: self.bind_target_area(area), accepting every u16 including 0xFFFF. It does not resolve the target, move, transfer areas, write current area/position or mirror the saved command tuple.
operands: one required numeric area ID, complete u16 0..65535 including 0xFFFF, encoded big-endian
domain_notes: DSL requires exactly one integer argument, does not validate native area-table lengths or restrict the value to known business-area IDs, and does not accept AreaTarget::TargetPlayer. It is a statement with no return value, not an if condition. Every 1A hi lo layout decompiles to bind_target_area with its original ID bytes retained.

Unlike 06 mode 3, which invalidates actor+3208 to 0xFFFF, 1A immediately fills that cache with the adapted area ID. Later kind-3 resolution in 0x108538B0 calls 0x108689D0, which can fill an invalid cache from actor+2046; the two paths can therefore converge. Native connectivity handling may still choose an intermediate area, so this does not lock the next hop or force a direct transfer.

The handler does not write actor+2040, actor+2038, position, or saved command actor+3231/+3232/+3234, and does not insert resolution, movement or area-change actions. Opcode 19 only binds the already selected next area and remains native; no alternate set_destination or set_next_area method is introduced.

name: accepted-request flag equality
summary: Selector 0 compares the payload value with actor+2681, the accepted-request flag, and skips to else/end when unequal. DSL handle uses the value-1 form as part of the complete takeover protocol; it is not an independent mind-state test.
control_flow: may skip nested instructions and decode subtype 2

summary: Selector 0 computes a deterministic ratio from two native hash-like functions, compares it with a threshold list, and walks nested 0x1C body instructions. Selectors 1/2 are marker forms.

control_flow: conditional nested-body skip; selector 1/2 repeatedly advance to marker

summary: Selector 0 continues only when actor+1040 (entity status byte) is not 1; otherwise it scans to a 0x1F marker. Selector 1 is marker-aware.

name: target_angle_match
summary: Selector 0 requires current target kind actor+2581 == 1, arg1 actor+2582 == 0 and index actor+2584 != 0xFFFF, then computes the directed XZ angle to the bound player once relative to heading actor+164. The first source-order threshold satisfying angle <= (upper << 8) selects its body. Invalid targets and all-miss cases use the optional else or continue after the block. No state writes. DSL: match self.target_angle() { degrees => body; else => body; }, where numeric cases are inclusive upper bounds, not equality values.

case marker carrying an inclusive u8 angle upper bound

Directed angle convention: front 0 degrees, right 90, rear 180, left 270. Target binding, saved-position resolution, turning and extra area/alive/visibility checks are not inserted.

DSL accepts 0..360 degrees including decimals, rounds to the nearest 1.40625-degree step with midpoint ties upward, clamps values above 358.59375 degrees to byte 255 and diagnoses the effective upper bound. A 360-degree source case is not a catch-all; else also handles invalid targets.
The count requires 1..255 cases. Duplicate, descending and quantized-equal upper bounds retain source order without sorting or branch removal.

Decompiler emits exact degree multiples for all byte thresholds and preserves optional else, ordering and duplicate values. Only complete, count-consistent, losslessly representable layouts are recovered; other valid native layouts remain native(...).
DSL requires the argumentless match method self.target_angle(); the query has no state writes and keeps the original 0x20 encoding and behavior.

The multiplier is the float constant at 0x1182F56C, not a global-object field. These values are not per-player hate scores. DSL keeps native(...).

This reads the same +2696/+2708 recovery-meter pair replenished by 4E 00; 0x9A instead reads the foraging-related +2700/+2712 pair. Non-time consumption and replenishment paths prevent treating either as a fixed cooldown. Species-specific game identities remain unresolved.

DSL: if self.near_target_2d(n) { ... }.

a body-size floor widens the threshold for large monsters; 0x36 has no such floor

name: repeat-body-counter
summary: Selector 0 saves a byte count and body cursor in the actor-wide repeat slot; the count is interpreted as signed i8. Selector 1 decrements it and jumps back while the signed result is positive. Non-positive initial counts use a special scan to 24 02. There is only one counter/cursor pair, so nesting or reentry overwrites it. Current structure validation rejects opcode 0x24 even inside native(...), because execution and skip boundaries disagree.
operands: selector; selector 0 carries one byte interpreted as a signed repeat count
control_flow: selector 1 loops through actor+2632 while decremented i8 actor+2623 > 0; selector 0 with i8 count <= 0 scans to 24 02 and may skip a following 24 01

decrement and loop while signed count remains positive
native scanner consumes only opcode; executed handler consumes opcode plus selector

domain_notes: The handler and native skip-length helper disagree for selectors other than 0/1: the handler consumes the selector, while the scanner advances only one byte. A structured repeat implementation must account for this protocol.
Count bytes 0x80..0xFF follow the non-positive entry path rather than representing 128..255 iterations.
Any future repeat syntax must restrict or validate nesting, shared-slot reentry and marker scanning; no repeat syntax is currently supported.
Recognition by the byte codec does not imply installability: ScriptStructure::push rejects every opcode 0x24 form, including native(...) escapes.

name: reset-repeat-counter
summary: Clears the actor-wide repeat count actor+2623 used by 0x24. It does not transfer the cursor out of the current body; a following 24 01 decrements zero to 0xFF and does not loop. DSL keeps native(...).

domain_notes: This is not a standalone break instruction; statements between 0x25 and the loop marker are not skipped by this opcode.

name: write-automatic-response-gate
summary: Writes the full u8 payload to actor+2738. Some automatic-event helpers require this byte to be zero, while awareness/automatic-attack response paths run when it is not one. Values other than 0/1 therefore cannot be collapsed into a boolean meaning. DSL keeps native(...).
domain_notes: 0x10858390/0x10858420/0x108584C0 require actor+2738 == 0 before setting event bit 0x80 and requesting interpreter restart.
The per-frame awareness path skips 0x108552C0 when actor+2738 == 1 and also gates an automatic switch to attack mode on actor+2738 != 1.
The full value domain and all reaction categories are unresolved; this is not the normal/attack mode field.

name: ordered-runtime-byte branch
summary: Compares the unresolved runtime byte actor+27 against an ordered byte list and skips nested 0x27 instructions according to the result. This byte has not been established as a linked-actor pointer.
operands: selector; selector 0 carries count and ordered byte list

variants.summary: logical count header; followed by a separate selector-1 branch marker and its u8 operand

domain_notes: variants.length records the logical linear instruction width; native_skip_length records the distinct 0x10860730 cursor increment, which includes the first branch marker for selector 0.

name: has_player_in_same_area
summary: Enters the body when some active player record shares the monster's raw area id at actor+2040, otherwise skips to else or end. No tracking, distance, line-of-sight, or map/day-night mapping is applied. DSL: self.has_player_in_same_area().
domain_notes: DSL requires empty parentheses for this argumentless if-condition method; there are no state writes or extra native operations.

name: area_timer_expired
summary: Enters the body when signed i16 actor+2910 is <= 0; positive values skip to else or end. Checks an area-related countdown without waiting, resetting it or initiating an area change. DSL: self.area_timer_expired.

name: attack_timer_active
summary: Enters the body when signed i16 actor+2912 is positive; otherwise skips to else or end. The timer decreases in attack mode, but this condition does not check the current mode. DSL: self.attack_timer_active.

name: field-equality branch
summary: Selector 0 compares one of nine runtime fields/actor-kind combinations with a payload byte and skips nested 0x2B body instructions when unequal.
operands: selector, comparison byte; selector 0 chooses field family via payload byte
domain_notes: Comparison behavior is confirmed; the field roles/value vocabulary remain unresolved to the same extent as the corresponding 0x0A or 0x0C/0x0D writer.

name: species-group branch
summary: Compares the normalized group key for actor species byte +3 with each case species through off_11A4E9C0, entering the first matching case; no match enters the optional fallback or ends the block.
operands: selector; selector 0 carries the case count, selector 1 carries a species ID
control_flow: ordered first-match branch with optional fallback

variants.summary: logical count header; followed by a separate selector-1 branch marker and its u8 operand

domain_notes: off_11A4E9C0 points to FF-terminated species groups; the opcode compares each group's first byte and preserves source order
variants.length records the logical linear instruction width; native_skip_length records the distinct 0x10860730 cursor increment, which includes the first branch marker for selector 0.

name: bind-scanned-object
summary: Publishes the ground object recorded by this frame's object scan as the action target: sets actor+2581 = 7 (target kind 7) and copies actor+2922/+2923 into actor+2582/+2584. The recorder keeps the triple cleared to 0xFF/0xFFFF when no in-area, same-height, unconsumed registry entry is found, so the commit can carry 'not found'. DSL: self.bind_scanned_object().
domain_notes: the recorded triple comes from the 32-slot ground-object registry dword_1ED8BE80 populated by sub_1141F790; recorders sub_10850880 (per-frame, entry distance + occlusion) and sub_10850A00 (same area/height, nearest, optional limit); sub_1085BFE0 consumes the entry (entry+0x13 = 1) and clears the record; target kind 7 resolves through sub_108538B0 case 7

This opcode only binds the recorded target. Native action helper 0x10850B80 separately binds/resolves kind 7 when local, calls 0x1085C010 for consumption/effects, then adds its amount to +2700 capped at +2712. 0x1085BFE0 only marks the bound registry entry consumed and clears the record; it does not perform meter replenishment or HP/status effects.

name: select-perception-profile
summary: Points actor+1968 at record n of the species perception-parameter table (32-byte records: max/min distance, height band above/below, half-angle in 1/65536 turn, and two distance thresholds). The index is species-private with no bounds check and can be overridden by species runtime conditions. DSL: self.select_perception_profile(n).
domain_notes: the 32-byte record fields are consumed by the per-frame awareness pass sub_108728A0; per-species table lengths measured 1..6 records, so the same index means different profiles per species

name: any_player_carrying
summary: Enters the body if any configured player's carry-state low nibble is nonzero, otherwise skips to else or end. No area, distance, target or item-category check. DSL: context.any_player_carrying().
domain_notes: DSL requires empty parentheses for this argumentless if-condition method; there are no state writes or extra native operations.

name: request-player-carry-response
summary: If any configured player has a nonzero low nibble in its carry-state byte, sets actor+3190 to 1. The request dispatcher later consumes this pending flag at priority 0x70 and obtains the request ID from the species table. Does not select a player, test area/distance or immediately execute a reaction. DSL keeps native(...).
control_flow: linear pending-request update; no script transfer or target binding
reads: player+1732 carry-state low nibble; player base 0x1DC6B750, stride 4176
writes: actor+3190=1 when any configured player is carrying
domain_notes: The scanned byte at 0x1DC6BE14 + 4176*i is player[i]+1732, not a generic lane-availability flag.
No match leaves the pending flag unchanged; this opcode does not clear a previously pending request.
The same carry-state predicate drives 0x2F; the resulting request/reaction ID is species-specific.

name: bind-cached-object-point
summary: Sets only target kind actor+2581 to 8. When the target is subsequently resolved, kind 8 copies the cached point actor+2864/+2868/+2872 into the target reference position. The point comes from a separate object-point scan and is not established as a home or spawn position. DSL keeps native(...).
control_flow: linear target-kind update; does not scan, resolve or move
domain_notes: The cached point is written by 0x10856A10 scanning the 32-slot registry at 0x1ECB1680 with area/species/range filters.
This registry is distinct from the ground-object registry 0x1ED8BE80 used by 0x2D; 0x31 does not refresh the cache itself.

name: actor-kind-pair gate
summary: Selector 0 compares actor bytes +20 and +21 against two payload bytes and walks nested 0x34 body instructions when either differs.

name: rage-active condition
summary: Selector 0 executes the body when the rage flag at actor+2726 is nonzero; otherwise it scans nested 0x35 blocks to else/end.

name: near-target-3d-gate
summary: Selector 0 compares the 3D distance between the actor position (+172/+176/+180) and the stored reference point (+2852/+2856/+2860) with operand * 100 and enters the nested body when the distance does not exceed it; selector 1 skips to the terminator, selector 2 ends the block. DSL: if self.near_target_3d(n) { ... }.

name: global-flag gate
summary: Selector 0 continues only when global object flags +44 do not contain bit 0x200000; otherwise it walks nested 0x37 body instructions.

name: area-context table gate
summary: Selector 0 reads off_1186916C using current area actor+2040 and actor+2008; a nonzero table byte suppresses the nested 0x38 body. The table role and actor+2008 context meaning are not established by this gate.

name: flash-active condition
summary: Selector 0 executes the body when the flash timer at actor+2914 is nonzero; otherwise it scans nested 0x39 blocks to else/end.

name: nonzero-selection gate
summary: Selector 0 continues only when actor+3186 is nonzero; otherwise it walks nested 0x3A body instructions.

name: null-pointer gate
summary: Selector 0 continues only when actor+3172 (linked-actor pointer) is null; otherwise it walks nested 0x3B body instructions.
domain_notes: +3172 = linked-actor pointer; sub_108578A0 scans the 3824-byte record array dword_1ED7AD2C (40 entries) for a record whose +3 equals a per-species constant and stores it here, 0 = none

name: other-actor gate
summary: Selector 0 suppresses the nested body only when actor+3172 points to another actor whose mode actor+2680 equals 1 and whose current area actor+2040 matches this actor.

name: start-area-path-script
summary: Normalizes a destination area ID, selects a matching outgoing area route (or the nearest route for 0xFFFF), chooses a route-entry step and binds target kind 9. Saves the caller continuation and transfers to root[12][entry-script]. The final byte is a line-probe height: multiplied by 10 and added to both probe endpoints' y coordinates, not a search radius. DSL keeps native(...).
operands: big-endian u16 destination area ID (0xFFFF selects nearest route), u8 probe-height units of 10
control_flow: returns the continuation for same-area, prohibited or unmatched-route cases; otherwise saves it at actor+2648 and returns root[12][entry-script], or null when that script table is absent

variants.summary: opcode plus big-endian destination area and u8 probe-height units

domain_notes: 0x11633C6C is the float constant 10.0; 0x10863DE3 and 0x10863E0E add the scaled operand to the two y coordinates passed to 0x108D0360.
In the current player area the handler tests eligible route-entry points with the line probe; outside that area it selects an eligible entry by horizontal distance.
The continuation is after all three payload bytes, and the entry-script index comes from route-step record +18; this is a native script call/transfer, not merely target selection.
The handler clears actor+2734 and stores actor+3201 even on early continuation paths; the complete role of actor+2734 remains unresolved.
